decision.durableContinuationPlan: Require an explicitly versioned durable recovery continuation artifact (`moriarty-recovery-continuation/1`, adapting major3's `Pending3` / `Closed3` persistence discipline to the paired L03 architecture) as a mandatory extension before claiming stage-continuation or CLI completion. The durable object must bind: (1) canonical digests of both the base Core/2 Program/StagePlan (`M03`) and the paired `RecoveryModuleView`/`RecoveryPlanView` (once the designated security owner adopts the paired digest preimage rule); (2) the current `ControlView` (`pending` carrying the exact `moriarty-continuation/1` object, or terminal `forward-complete` / `recovery-complete` snapshots); (3) the cumulative `AccountingView` (`profile: "moriarty-local-recovery-accounting/1"`, `committed`, `attempted_total`, `committed_cap`, and full `ordered_effects`); and (4) bounded `history: [InvocationView]` (at most 256 invocations). Decoding must enforce the existing strict JSON discipline (`deny_unknown_fields`, canonical `UInt` strings, 4 MiB continuation ceiling, 64 KiB event ceiling, and combined `canonical_boundary` validation). Bare `moriarty-continuation/1` files lack `attempted_total` and `ordered_effects` and must never be silently imported as if they possessed complete lifetime accounting.
decision.firstImplementationScope: After two agreeing non-author design votes, designated security owner review of paired identity/admission/error premises, and an independent non-author custodian freeze of all expected artifacts, the first implementation slice is the SDK-free Rust library module `mori_core::stage::recovery` (`load`, `start`, `RecoveryProgram::view`, `RecoveryProcess::{resume, recover, report}`) plus paired static validation, planning, and unit/integration tests over finite specimens A (custody refund with retained fee and unrelated warranty residual), B (forward compensation from insurer/reserve with positive residual duty and `successful_path_ceiling = 17 > forward_total = 13`), C (deadline-reached with `outcome_known = false` remaining pending and charging attempted guard work `4`), and D (failed handler body retaining prior committed prefix and charging attempted work `6`). This first slice must be explicitly labeled an in-memory local-reference-stage foundation and must not claim `MPLR-002`, `C1.1`, CLI recovery, or target completion.
decision.minimalCoherentInterface: Pair an unmodified `language "moriarty/2";` agreement (`moriarty-core/2`) with a first-class companion recovery language module (`recovery "moriarty-recovery/1"; for agreement <Id>; on action <Id> at await <Id> { (refund|compensate) <handler>(<binders>) when <guard> { <OrdinaryStmt>* } }`) under transition semantics `moriarty-core2-recovery/1`. Expose `mori_core::stage::recovery::{load, start}` returning `RecoveryProgram` (`view() -> RecoveryProgramView`) and opaque `RecoveryProcess` (`resume`, `recover`, `report() -> RecoveryProcessReport`), with typed `RecoveryEvent` (`moriarty-recovery-event/1`) and `RecoveryErrorView` (`moriarty-local-recovery-error/1`). Each handler allocates its guard and body expressions in a handler-local arena (`0..m`) without shifting base `Program.expressions`; `RecoverySegment` records `guard: {root, value, snapshot, effects: []}` separately and emits ordinary `Statement` steps at `0..n-1`. Paired `load`/`start` must validate combined base+handler liability registries, require explicit boundary balance rows for all accounts referenced in recovery handler `Transfer`/`Fee` statements, enforce `MAX_TRACE_CELLS <= 65,536` across recovery branches, and preflight `committed_cap` against `RecoveryActionPlan.successful_path_ceiling`.
decision.publicCliAndSourcePlan: Preserve inspectable source authoring via the explicit two-module pair (`moriarty/2` base `.mori` file plus `moriarty-recovery/1` companion `.mori` file, parsed independently with no syntax-stripping preprocessor). Extend public `mori simulate` (and `mori test` under a versioned test manifest profile) with explicit flags `--recovery-module <FILE>` and mutually exclusive `--recover <FILE> --recovery-event <FILE>` (conflicting with `--resume`, `--scenario`, `--trace`, `--target`, and signed replay arguments, following `simulate.rs` Clap discipline) that read/write the durable recovery continuation and render deterministic ASCII JSON reports (`qualification: "local-reference-stage"`, `authentication: "none"`, `consumption: "untracked"`). Retain `major3` inline `recover refund|compensate` syntax as an optional future frontend sugar lowering to the same paired IR if single-file ergonomics are later prioritized.
decision.reason: `L03_WITH_REQUIRED_EXTENSIONS` is the smallest coherent design that satisfies inspectable source-bound pending recovery without mutating or duplicating the frozen `moriarty/2` / `moriarty-core/2` stack. Unlike in-place `/2` mutation (which breaks frozen `M01` `ExprId`s, `M03` hashes, byte-identical false-resume `moriarty-continuation/1` tokens, and `outcome_report` key sets) and unlike full `major3` (which forks the entire normal `Program3`/`Action3`/`Statement3`/`StagePlan3`/`Execution3` family, shifts forward suffix `ExprId`s when inline recovery arms are edited, and injects a synthetic `RecoveryGate3` statement at Step 0 shifting body steps to `1..n`), `L03` keeps forward Core/2 untouched while giving recovery its own inspectable grammar (`moriarty-recovery/1`), handler-local expression arenas, clean guard metadata, and `0..n-1` body `Step`s. However, because a library-only increment is not completion, `L03` must be paired with mandatory extensions for: (1) a versioned durable public recovery-continuation wire format and decoder, (2) public `mori simulate` / `mori test` CLI recovery integration, and (3) combined base+recovery static boundary/account/liability-registry/trace-cell validation at `load`/`start`.

The companion recovery language uses header `moriarty-recovery/1`, transition semantics `moriarty-core2-recovery/1`, program view `moriarty-recovery-program/1`, plan view `moriarty-recovery-plan/1`, event format `moriarty-recovery-event/1`, report format `moriarty-local-recovery/1`, accounting profile `moriarty-local-recovery-accounting/1`, and error format `moriarty-local-recovery-error/1` (plus a required versioned durable continuation format `moriarty-recovery-continuation/1` for CLI persistence). financialAssessment.conditionalFailureVariants: Verified both L04 failure variants and Example D: (1) `failure_before_any_new_financial_effect` (`pool[58]` / `pool[125]`, and Example D where `insurer` has `10 < 20` PAY): no remedy transfer, fee, or discharge commits; `financial_post` equals `complete_pending` (`pool[37]` / `pool[101]`); prior committed effects (`Fee 4` + `Transfer 60` + `Liability 60` in custody-refund; `Fee 3` + `Transfer 40` + `Liability 20` in forward-compensation; `Fee 2` + `Transfer 50` + `Liability 50` in Example D) and all positive duties remain intact; under L03/major3 local reference semantics (`qualification: "local-reference-stage"`), a failed handler body is locally atomic and charges attempted work (`4 + 2 = 6` in D, giving `C = 7, T = 13`). (2) `failure_after_remedy_transfer_before_discharge` (`pool[57]` / `pool[124]`): models a conditional non-atomic target-phase failure where the remedy `Transfer` (`60` `escrow -> buyer` in `pool[41]`/`pool[42]`, or `12` `reserve -> buyer` in `pool[105]`/`pool[109]`) commits while the subsequent `Discharge` does not, leaving `custody-refund: 60` (`pool[36]`) or `remedy: 20` (`pool[100]`) undischarged. As L04 specifies, payment alone must never infer discharge, and the transfer must not be replayed as if absent; reachability, committed/attempted counters, and late-event handling under partial-commit phases remain unspecified until owner phase policy is adopted.

financialAssessment.forwardCompensation: Independently verified both `L03`/`major3` Example B/C and `L04` `forward-compensation` (`pool[127]`): In Example B (`PAY`, `marker: 77`, opening `alice: 100, insurer: 30, merchant: 0, observer: 7, treasury: 0`, total `137`, no opening duties), prefix (`Fee 2`, `Transfer 50` to `merchant`, `Liability remedy 50` `insurer -> alice`, `Await acknowledgement` entry `1`; `C = 7, T = 7`) leaves `alice: 48, insurer: 30, merchant: 50, observer: 7, treasury: 2` and `remedy: 50`. Remedy transfers `12` from `reserve` (`30 -> 18`) to `buyer` (`157 -> 169`) and discharges `remedy` `20 -> 8` (`pool[115]`), preserving `supplier: 48` (original `8` + payment `40`), `treasury: 5` (retained fee `3`), `buyer` gross `43` and net debit `31`, `reserve` gross debit `12`, and closing positive residuals `[audit: 4 BOND, remedy: 8 PAY]` (`pool[114]`).
financialAssessment.unresolvedAndOverheadUnknowns: In `L04` (`pool[61]`, `pool[63]`, `L04/MISSING-PREMISES.json`, `L04/FREEZE.json`), the ordinary prefix costs `7` (`fee 2 + transfer 2 + liability 2 + await entry 1`), the normal false guard costs `2` (`dispatch 1 + Name 1`, `committed` unchanged at `7`), and the standalone two-statement remedy body (`Transfer 2 + Discharge 2`, without `Emit`) costs `4` if run as an ordinary `/2` action. Their arithmetic sum `7 + 2 + 4 = 13` is explicitly NOT a recovery lifetime meter: (1) false-guard attempts (`2`) increase `attempted_total` (`T`) but never `committed` (`C`); (2) a real recovery transition adds the recovery handler's own guard cost (`1 + nodes(guard)`) and any `Emit` statement (`2`); and (3) standalone `/2` actions leave the original pending frame (`fund` with captured `principal: 60` or `purchase` with captured `remedy: 20`) unconsumed (`specific_pending_frame_gap`). In `L04`, recovery dispatch/overhead, cumulative committed/attempted recovery counters, failure attempted work, cap/refusal precedence, late-event/race disposition, and external/native fees remain explicitly `UNSPECIFIED`. Under `L03`/`major3`, ordinary local logical work equations are specified (`C' = C + guard_cost + body_cost` on recovery success; `C' = C, T' = T + attempted` on false/rejected), while physical memory/CPU envelopes, native circuit costs, DUST/ledger fees, and phase-failure charges remain owner-dependent unknowns.

findings.evidence: `L03/README.md` ("The first scope is a public in-memory library capability, not a new serialized resume-token migration or CLI cancellation claim") and `L03/INTERFACE-AND-RUNTIME.md` ("Initial scope is the public library consumer plus ordinary tests. Existing `mori simulate` file start/resume remains unchanged"), contrasted with `MPLR-002` (`partial-conditional-transactions/spec.md:14-24`), `C1.1` (`tasks.md:16`), `UNI-024` (`consolidated-language-kernel/spec.md:286-300`), `current/crates/mori/src/commands/simulate.rs:18-28,177-206`, and `major3/DESIGN.md` (`Pending3` / `moriarty-continuation/2`, `Closed3`, and `mori simulate --recover FILE --recovery-event FILE`).
findings.requiredChange: Do not treat the in-memory `RecoveryProcess` library increment as completion of staged recovery. Require a versioned durable recovery continuation wire format (`moriarty-recovery-continuation/1` carrying paired base+recovery digests, embedded `moriarty-continuation/1`, `AccountingView`, and bounded `history`) and public `mori simulate` / `mori test` CLI recovery support as mandatory follow-on deliverables before closing `MPLR-002`, `MPLR-005`, `C0.1`, `C1.1`, or `C3.2`.

findings.evidence: `current/crates/mori-core/src/stage/decode.rs:56-81,98-234` checks `registry(p)` (`lines 56-81`), required balance accounts (`lines 161-184`), and `MAX_TRACE_CELLS = 65_536` (`lines 221-233`) only against base `p.actions[action].statements`. In Example B (`CompensationExample`), `"insurer"` appears in base `buy()` only in `Liability("remedy", PAY, "insurer", "alice", 50)` and is only debited via `Transfer` inside the recovery handler (`L03/GRAMMAR-AND-IR.md`, `L03/PREDICATES-AND-CUSTODY.md`), and similarly for `"reserve"` in `L04` `forward-compensation` (`L04/forward-compensation/primitive-actions.proposed.mori:9-19`). Thus unmodified `stage::start` (`decode::canonical_boundary`) does not check that `"insurer"` or `"reserve"` has an explicit `PAY` balance row at start! Furthermore, `L03/GRAMMAR-AND-IR.md` allows handlers to declare new liabilities and requires all handler accounts to exist in the input boundary.
findings.requiredChange: In `mori_core::stage::recovery::load` and `start` (and durable continuation decoding), enforce combined static and boundary admission before invoking `stage::start`: (1) build a unified liability identity registry across all base actions and all `RecoveryModule` handlers, rejecting any conflicting `(asset, debtor, creditor)` identity for the same duty name; (2) require explicit canonical balance rows in the opening/pending `Snapshot` for every `(asset, account)` referenced by `Transfer` or `Fee` in any recovery handler bound to the selected action; and (3) check `MAX_TRACE_CELLS` (`65,536`) across every recovery handler arm including handler-created liabilities.

findings.evidence: `current/crates/mori-core/src/stage/cost.rs:176-228` (`start_preflight` checks `plan.plan_total > cap`, and `resume_preflight` checks `committed + segment_cost > effective_cap`). In Example B (`L03/PREDICATES-AND-CUSTODY.md`), base `plan_total` is `13` (`prefix 7 + suffix 6`), whereas the recovery path total is `17` (`prefix 7 + guard 4 + body 6 = 17`), so `RecoveryActionPlan.successful_path_ceiling` is `17`. Calling unmodified `stage::start` with `cap = Some(15)` would pass base `start_preflight` (`13 <= 15`) even though `15 < 17`.
findings.requiredChange: Specify that `mori_core::stage::recovery::start` performs paired preflight checking `committed_cap >= RecoveryActionPlan.successful_path_ceiling` (`max(forward_total, max_arm(committed_before(site) + guard_cost + body_cost))`) before calling `stage::start`, and `RecoveryProcess::recover` performs recovery preflight checking `invocation_cap <= stored_cap` (when `stored_cap` is present) and `committed_before(site) + recovery_cost <= effective_cap` before evaluating the recovery guard.

findings.evidence: `major3/DESIGN.md` allocates inline recovery arm expressions inside the single global `Program3.expressions` arena before the forward suffix and emits a synthetic `RecoveryGate3{arm, guard}` statement at route-local `Step.index = 0` with body statements shifted to `1..n`. By contrast, `current/docs/CORE-STAGED-TESTS.md:175-186,237-293` (`M01` and Core/2 observation contract) freezes 0-based `Step.index` over ordinary `Statement` variants and global expression numbering for `moriarty/2`, which `L03/GRAMMAR-AND-IR.md` and `L03/INTERFACE-AND-RUNTIME.md` preserve via handler-local expression arenas (`0..m`), separate `RecoverySegment.guard` metadata, and `0..n-1` ordinary body `Step`s.
findings.requiredChange: Adopt `L03`'s handler-local expression arena (`0..m`), separate `RecoverySegment.guard: {root, value, snapshot, effects: []}` observation field, and `0..n-1` ordinary `Statement` body `Step`s rather than `major3`'s inline global arena shifting and synthetic `RecoveryGate3` step. If inline `moriarty/3` syntax is ever added later as authoring sugar, lower its recovery arms into per-handler arenas and separate guard metadata rather than mutating forward `ExprId`s or inventing synthetic gate statements.

findings.evidence: `L04/README.md:14`, `L04/DERIVATION.md:27-33`, `L04/MISSING-PREMISES.json`, and `L04-LOSSLESS-TREES.json` (`pool[63]`: `"arithmetic_sum_of_chosen_operation_work": "7+2+4=13; NOT a normative recovery lifetime counter"`). `L04` models standalone 2-statement primitive remedy actions (`Transfer` + `Discharge` = `4` units) without a recovery guard or `Emit` statement and sums `7` (prefix) + `2` (false guard) + `4` (body) = `13`.
findings.requiredChange: When adapting `L04`'s `custody-refund` and `forward-compensation` economic specimens into companion `moriarty-recovery/1` test cases, preserve all `L04` opening/pending/post snapshots, preserved accounts (`escrow: 5` PAY, `BOND` cells), unrelated `audit: 4` BOND duty, and failure boundaries, but never use `4` or `13` as a recovery lifetime work meter; compute `committed` (`C`) and `attempted_total` (`T`) strictly from the paired recovery guard/body schedule and keep missing phase-failure/overhead rules explicitly owner-dependent.

scopeAssessment.attemptedCommittedAccounting: `L03` (`AccountingView`) and `major3` (`Accounting3`) specify the exact same sound local equations over checked `UInt128`: on a successful segment/handler of cost `k` (`attempted t = k`), `C' = C + k`, `T' = T + t`, and `E' = E ++ new_effects`; on a false guard or rejected handler with attempted work `t`, `C' = C`, `T' = T + t`, and `E' = E` (with pre-evaluation refusals charging `t = 0`). `L03` cleanly keeps `T` and `E` in the outer `RecoveryProcess` / durable recovery continuation so the embedded `moriarty-continuation/1` remains byte-for-byte unchanged on a false normal resume, while `RecoveryActionPlan.successful_path_ceiling` bounds maximum committed work along any single successful path (`15` in A, `17` in B) without conflating that committed ceiling with lifetime `attempted_total` (`T = 17` in A and `T = 21` in B after a false guard).
scopeAssessment.completeEffectsDuties: Both `L03` and `major3` preserve complete post-statement snapshots (all declared states, canonical `(asset, account)` balance rows including untouched observer/operator/BOND accounts, and canonical liability rows distinguishing absent from `present-zero`), append every new statement delta to `ordered_effects` (`E`) without netting refunds against prior gross debits or erasing retained fees (`fee 2` in A/B, `fee 4` and `fee 3` in L04), and compute positive `residual` liabilities (`amount > 0`) separately from control closure (`warranty: 9` in A; `remedy: 30` in B; `audit: 4` BOND in L04 custody-refund; `audit: 4` BOND and `remedy: 8` PAY in L04 forward-compensation).
scopeAssessment.failurePhases: Both proposals properly distinguish local reference evaluator rejection (`qualification: "local-reference-stage"`, where a failed handler body such as Example D discards uncommitted working changes, emits `segment: null` and `status: "rejected"`, preserves prior committed state/effects/fees/duties `C = 7`, and adds attempted handler work `T = 7 + 6 = 13`) from actual Midnight ledger phase execution (`UNI-006`, `MPLR-009`, `MORIARTY-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md:47`), where guaranteed-phase fees or partial prefixes (such as L04's conditional `failure_after_remedy_transfer_before_discharge` in `pool[57]`/`pool[124]`) may commit without discharging liabilities. Local handler atomicity is never lowered as a ledger rollback assumption.
scopeAssessment.noLibraryOnlyScopeWaiver: An in-memory library wrapper (`RecoveryProcess` alone) does not complete the staged recovery requirement (`MPLR-002`, `MPLR-005`, `C0.1`, `C1.1`, `C3.2`, `UNI-008`, `UNI-024`). While `L03`'s `mori_core::stage::recovery` is the right minimal first implementation slice, original obligations for inspectable language sources, versioned durable public continuations, public `mori simulate` / `mori test` CLI operation, independent non-author custodian freezes, and full target/ZKIRv3/Midnight phase and proof correspondence remain mandatory and unwaived.
scopeAssessment.pendingClosure: Both `L03` and `major3` bind recovery handlers statically in source to a specific `(action, await_label / site)` and evaluate the selected handler against the actual pending boundary and captured `Input`/`Let`/prior-`Event` slots. On normal handler completion, control transitions to `recovery-complete` with no pending forward successor, retiring the forward suffix (e.g., merchant delivery in A) for that workflow instance, whereas a standalone ordinary `/2` action (`L04` `specific_pending_frame_gap`) leaves the original pending continuation open and unconsumed. Subsequent `resume` or `recover` calls on a `recovery-complete` process are rejected as `not-pending` with `attempted = 0` and no state change.
scopeAssessment.refundVsCompensation: Both proposals and `L04` maintain a strict semantic and accounting distinction between `refund` (returning still-controlled principal from modeled custody, e.g., `escrow -> alice 60` in A and `escrow -> buyer 60` in L04 while preserving `escrow`'s unrelated `5` PAY and `7` BOND and retaining prior fees) and `compensate` (executing a new forward transfer from a third-party/reserve remedy source after payment has already committed to `merchant`/`supplier`, e.g., `insurer -> alice 20` in B leaving `merchant: 50` and `remedy: 30`, or `reserve -> buyer 12` in L04 leaving `supplier: 48` and `remedy: 8`).
